question: Can an explicit class hierarchy be embedded more faithfully by regularizing supervised visual representations with Poincare distances and a rooted centering constraint, and does that geometry improve classification and OOD detection?

key_findings.claim: HypStructure extends Euclidean CPCC by correlating tree distances with Poincare distances between hyperbolic class prototypes and adds a root-centering loss.
key_findings.evidence: Features are mapped or clipped into a Poincare ball, prototypes for leaves and internal nodes are formed using Klein/Einstein averaging, and all node-pair geodesic distances enter CPCC. A second term pulls the global/root prototype to the origin. The composite objective can use SupCon, hyperbolic SupCon, or a hyperbolic network, with stated batch complexity O(d min(b^2,k^2)).

key_findings.claim: The method substantially improves hierarchy-shape metrics, while ordinary classification gains are mostly modest and not uniformly aligned with test CPCC.
key_findings.evidence: Across CIFAR10/100 and ImageNet100, relative hyperbolicity falls from flat values 0.232/0.209/0.168 to 0.094/0.127/0.134. Fine kNN accuracy improves over flat by 0.15, 1.72, and 0.11 points respectively. On CIFAR100, however, test CPCC is 0.766 versus 0.779 for Euclidean CPCC, showing that lower Gromov distortion and classification can improve even when the named hierarchy-correlation metric does not.

key_findings.claim: Hierarchy-aware training gives strong OOD results with a simple Mahalanobis score, but gains vary sharply by dataset and nearly vanish on ImageNet100 average AUROC.
key_findings.evidence: Average AUROC is 97.75 on CIFAR10, 88.81 on CIFAR100, and 93.83 on ImageNet100. These beat the strongest tabulated comparators by 0.37, 1.14, and only 0.02 points respectively; HypStructure also loses individual cells such as CIFAR100 Textures/iSUN and ImageNet100 Textures/iNaturalist. All results use far-OOD datasets and one primary Mahalanobis feature score rather than near-OOD or FPR95 calibration.

key_findings.claim: The component ablations support internal nodes, hyperbolic prototypes, and centering, though several design choices and the hierarchy itself are not stress-tested.
key_findings.evidence: On CIFAR100, adding centering to the internal-node/hyperbolic-centroid variant raises fine accuracy from 76.22 to 76.91; removing internal nodes or hyperbolic centroids reduces performance. Weighted CIFAR10 trees visibly alter distances as requested, and alternate flat losses/backbones retain gains. There is no experiment with incorrect, incomplete, automatically inferred, imbalanced, or adversarial hierarchies despite this being the main acknowledged dependency.

key_findings.claim: The eigenspectrum theorem characterizes an ideal block-constant Gram matrix, not the representations produced by the implemented regularizer or a proved cause of OOD improvement.
key_findings.evidence: The analysis assumes CPCC reaches one, every sample acts as a tree leaf, all normalized pair similarities sharing an ancestor height are identical, labels are balanced for the closed form, and Poincare points have effectively equal clipped norms. Training instead regularizes class prototypes, reports CPCC below one, and can use exponential maps with unequal radii. The OOD link is an empirical top-principal-component plot; the theorem contains no OOD distribution or detection-error bound.

anchors.section: A Details of Eigenspectrum Analysis, Setup

method.core_idea: Make supervised features respect known semantic tree distances in a geometry whose volume growth naturally represents branching hierarchies.
method.mechanism: Compute class and internal-node prototypes in a Poincare ball, maximize the Pearson correlation between all prototype geodesic distances and tree shortest-path distances, center the root at the origin, and combine these terms with a standard classification or contrastive objective.
assumptions: A reliable tree over all target labels is available or cheaply constructible.
Shortest-path distance in that tree is a meaningful target for visual representation distance.
Batch prototypes adequately estimate each class distribution.
Constant negative curvature is suitable across all branches and hierarchy depths.
Far-OOD separation induced by the hierarchy transfers to unseen datasets.

techniques.role: Correlates tree distances with Poincare geodesic distances between prototypes.
Aggregates class and internal-node embeddings in hyperbolic geometry.
Places the root near the Poincare origin and encourages descendants toward the boundary.
Includes internal hierarchy nodes rather than only leaf classes.
Models ideal hierarchy-aligned similarities as nested block matrices.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet100 with ResNet-18/34
evaluations.metric: relative Gromov hyperbolicity, test CPCC, fine/coarse kNN accuracy
evaluations.result: relative distortion improves 20-59%; fine accuracy improves 0.11-1.72 points over flat SupCon

evaluations.setting: Far-OOD detection across 5 CIFAR and 4 ImageNet100 OOD datasets
evaluations.result: average AUROC 97.75, 88.81, and 93.83 for CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet100
evaluations.baseline: SSD+, KNN+, CIDER, CSI, ProxyAnchor, CE+SimCLR, and Euclidean CPCC

evaluations.result: all internal nodes, hyperbolic centroids, and centering give best fine/coarse accuracy 76.91/86.22

evaluations.setting: Alternative hyperbolic SupCon loss and clipped hyperbolic backbone
evaluations.result: HypStructure retains improvements under both variants
evaluations.baseline: the corresponding hyperbolic flat objective without structure regularization

evaluations.metric: Gram eigenvalues and AUROC using top-k principal components
evaluations.result: structured methods show a gap near 20 coarse classes; HypStructure's top 20 components are most OOD-informative
evaluations.baseline: flat SupCon and Euclidean CPCC spectra

limitations: Requires a supplied class tree whose errors or biases are directly imposed on features.
Only three small-to-medium image benchmarks and shallow three-level hierarchies are tested.
Primary classification gains are modest outside CIFAR100.
OOD evaluation emphasizes far-OOD AUROC and omits near-OOD, FPR95, AUPR, calibration, and semantic-shift stress tests.
Only three random seeds are reported, with no statistical hypothesis tests for small gains.
Constant curvature, hierarchy weights, and regularization strengths are mostly fixed manually.
The eigenspectrum theory depends on ideal conditions not guaranteed by CPCC training.
failure_modes: A wrong parent-child relation forces semantically dissimilar visual classes together or related classes apart.
Unbalanced or locally non-tree taxonomies can be distorted by a single constant-curvature ball.
Mini-batches missing classes or internal branches yield noisy prototype and CPCC estimates.
Poincare boundary saturation can cause numerical instability and vanishing or exploding geodesic gradients.
A hierarchy that improves far-OOD clustering can worsen near-OOD rejection by making unseen siblings look in-distribution.
Class centroids can erase multimodal within-class structure even when the surrounding geometry is hyperbolic.
reusable_insights: Match representation geometry to known output structure instead of treating label IDs as exchangeable.
Regularize internal concepts as well as leaves when a hierarchy provides reliable higher-level supervision.
A root-position constraint resolves otherwise free hyperbolic translations and improves interpretability.
Evaluate hierarchy preservation, task accuracy, and OOD behavior separately because they need not move together.
Stress-test structure-aware models with perturbed and competing taxonomies before deploying inherited semantic assumptions.
open_questions: How robust is HypStructure to edge deletion, label noise, disputed taxonomies, and automatically induced hierarchies?
Can curvature vary by branch or be learned without losing stable optimization?
Would distributional distances such as optimal transport outperform prototypes while retaining hyperbolic low distortion?
Does hierarchy-aware geometry improve near-OOD and hierarchical open-set recognition under OpenOOD 1.5 protocols?
Can eigenspectrum or OOD guarantees be derived from finite CPCC and approximate, unequal-norm prototypes?
How does the method scale to ImageNet-1K, long-tailed taxonomies, multimodal foundation features, and millions of labels?

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Structured Representations by Embedding Class Hierarchy
competitive_landscape.difference: Zeng et al. correlate tree distances with Euclidean distances between leaf-class centroids; HypStructure moves CPCC to Poincare geometry, embeds internal nodes, and adds root centering and OOD analysis.

competitive_landscape.title: Hyperbolic Image Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Khrulkov et al. show implicit hierarchy and low-dimensional benefits for image classification/retrieval; HypStructure explicitly supplies a label tree and aligns its pairwise distances through a regularizer.

competitive_landscape.title: Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Yue et al. replace contrastive similarity with hyperbolic geometry without requiring an explicit taxonomy; HypStructure is an additive hierarchy loss and demonstrates compatibility with that hyperbolic contrastive objective.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Structured Representations by Embedding Class Hierarchy with Fast Optimal Transport
competitive_landscape.difference: OT-CPCC replaces centroid distance with approximate Earth Mover's Distance to preserve multimodal class distributions in Euclidean space; HypStructure attacks geometric tree distortion instead, while retaining centroid summaries.

competitive_landscape.title: Balanced Hyperbolic Embeddings Are Natural Out-of-Distribution Detectors
competitive_landscape.difference: Balanced Hyperbolic Learning separately optimizes taxonomy prototypes with distortion and branch-norm balancing, evaluates 13 datasets and 13 OOD scores including near-OOD/FPR95, and fixes prototypes during backbone training; HypStructure jointly regularizes batch prototypes through CPCC with broader representation-learning aims but a narrower OOD protocol.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The first explicit hyperbolic structured regularizer to embed label hierarchies, yielding low-distortion interpretable features, classification and OOD gains, plus a first eigenspectrum characterization of structured representations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Three vision benchmarks, nine far-OOD datasets, component and architecture/loss ablations, low-dimensional analyses, and idealized balanced/arbitrary-tree Gram-matrix theorems are provided.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Combining full-tree CPCC, hyperbolic prototypes, and centering is a clear and modular advance over Euclidean CPCC. The empirical hierarchy and CIFAR100 OOD gains are credible; classification gains are small, ImageNet100 OOD is effectively tied, and the elegant eigenspectrum analysis should be read as an ideal block-model explanation rather than a theorem about trained HypStructure features or OOD generalization.

reviewer_notes: Read all 40 pages, including proofs, implementation, component/geometry ablations, full OOD tables, reproducibility checklist, and limitations. Competitors were verified through primary ICLR/OpenReview, arXiv, and publisher records on 2026-08-23.
